chapter: Ellington colleagues, singers and world tours
title: George Simon's profile: crooner, symphony, his father
summary: Brown corrects claims that he crooned, that his father taught him instruments, and says he played symphony in school and at CBS.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: In George Simon's book work, Simon Says, there's a paragraph on various members of the Ellington band, April, 1937, and it's not clear whether it's -- the information comes from George Simon or from Duke Ellington, but about Lawrence Brown, trombone Congo, it says, 'a crooner at heart.' What do
you have to say about that?
You see, I never sang a note since I was about 12 years old. I used to sing in the kiddie -- kids' choir and things like that, but not professionally or anything like that.
Oh, in the early days in school, yes, we had very -- very good symphony orchestras, full symphonies, and, of course, played some symphony in the CBS staff.
In school, was that where you were playing trombone, or were you --
And it says here, "His dad, a Topeka minister, taught him every instrument except trombone."
No, he didn't teach me any instrument. He allowed me to take the instruments, as I before mentioned, in schools of California. That's the only place. No, he didn't teach anything except Bible class.
